name: Rest meditation wide
prompt: A trail runner, wearing loose, fully-covering outdoor running layers (long sleeves, leggings or joggers), sits cross-legged on a thick bed of green moss in a fern-filled clearing just off a forest trail, facing the camera, hands resting loosely on the knees, spine tall and relaxed, shoulders soft, eyes gently closed the entire time, their face clearly visible and unobstructed: cheeks and forehead slightly flushed from exertion, with a calm, contented, quietly fulfilled half-smile, breathing slowly and deeply, the chest and shoulders rising gently on each inhale and settling softly on each exhale, a faint hint of breath in the cool air. Framed as a wide shot showing the whole seated figure with plenty of the clearing, ferns and river around them. Ferns and moss all around them, tall evergreen trees surrounding the clearing, sunlight filtering through the canopy in soft dappled patches, a gentle river visible through the trees nearby, light morning mist drifting slowly between the trunks. Built to loop seamlessly: the clip begins and ends on the same moment, with the person at the very end of an exhale (chest settled, shoulders soft, eyes closed, hands resting on the knees, head level), and in between they take exactly one slow, deep breath, inhaling for about three seconds and exhaling for about three seconds, so the final frame matches the first frame in posture, framing and lighting. Apart from that breath, very subtle ambient motion only: leaves and ferns swaying slightly in a light breeze, mist drifting, light patches shimmering gently; the person stays seated and otherwise still, with no talking, no stretching and no opening of the eyes. Cinematic, polished outdoor lifestyle video, natural light, shallow depth of field, filmed from a single fixed camera position at eye level — the camera never moves, pans, or zooms and the subject never turns or changes position. Constant, even lighting with no sun flares, no camera or exposure changes, and no objects entering or leaving the frame, so the last frame is nearly identical to the first. Vertical video, about 6 seconds, one continuous shot, photorealistic, G-rated, no on-screen text or watermark.
